info.title: Child Digital Care API
info.description:
Backend API for **Child Digital Care**: an Android-first parental-control and
family digital-wellbeing platform.

This API is the single source of truth for three separately developed clients
(Parent App, Child App, Admin Dashboard). The clients never talk to each other
or to the database directly.

### What the server does and does not claim

The server stores policy *intent*, distributes typed commands, and records what
devices report back. It cannot enforce anything on an Android device. A rule is
only ever reported as applied because a device acknowledged applying it;
`unsupported` and `permission_denied` are first-class outcomes and are never
translated into success.

### Principals

| Principal | Audience | Obtained via |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent / guardian | `cdc:parent` | `POST /auth/login` |
| Child device | `cdc:device` | `POST /device/pairing/claim` |
| Admin | `cdc:admin` | `POST /admin/auth/login` |

A credential for one principal is rejected on another's routes.

### Conventions

* Every success response uses the envelope
  `{"success": true, "message": ..., "data": ..., "meta": {"request_id": ...}}`.
* Errors use `{"success": false, "error": {"code", "message", "details"}, "meta": ...}`
  with a stable machine-readable `code`.
* Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC; identifiers are UUIDs.
* Large collections use opaque cursor pagination.
* `Idempotency-Key` is honoured where a retry could otherwise duplicate work.

get.description:
Not ready unless the database is reachable.

Redis is reported but is not fatal on its own: with ``RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_OPEN``
the API still serves requests, and the outbox simply drains later.

Honest configuration report, so a client never has to guess whether a
feature will work. ``not_configured`` means calls will fail explicitly
rather than silently succeeding.

post.description:
Register a parent account and send a verification email.

The response is identical whether or not the address was already
registered, so this endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.

Exchange credentials for an access/refresh token pair.

Limited per IP *and* per hashed email. The per-account bucket is generous
and never locks the account, so an attacker cannot deny a victim access by
hammering their address.

Rotate the session.

The presented token is consumed. Presenting it again revokes the whole
token family (reuse detection) and returns ``REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED``.
Always reports success, whether or not the address exists.
Sets a new password and signs out every existing session.

get.summary: The signed-in parent and their families

delete.description: Scoped to the caller's own sessions, so one parent cannot sign another out.

get.description: Only families the caller is an active member of are returned.

post.description: The caller becomes the family owner and holds every family permission.

get.description:
A non-member receives 404, not 403: the existence of another tenant's
family must not be discoverable by guessing identifiers.

delete.description: The owner cannot be removed; ownership transfer is a separate flow.

post.description:
Family restructuring, billing and privacy permissions are never delegated:
they are stripped from the request before the invitation is stored.

The invitation is bound to the invited email address, so a leaked link
cannot be redeemed by a different account.

Stores an age band rather than a date of birth: the product does not
need an exact birthday, and collecting one would be unnecessary data about
a child.

get.summary: List child profiles in a family

delete.description:
Deactivates rather than hard-deletes.

Every linked device is unlinked and every pending pairing invitation is
revoked first, so monitoring stops immediately and no orphaned device keeps
a working credential. The usage history is kept until the retention window
elapses or an explicit deletion request is made, which is why this returns
a retention note rather than claiming the data is gone.

post.description:
Mint a short-lived, single-use pairing invitation.

``claim_token`` is returned **once**, here. The server stores only its
SHA-256 hash, so it cannot be retrieved again and never appears in a log.
Encode this token (not a parent JWT, and no account details) in the QR code.

get.summary: List pairing invitations for a child

get.description:
Scoped to the caller's families: an invitation id from another family is
reported as not found.

post.description:
Exchange a pairing invitation for a device-scoped credential.

This is the only unauthenticated write in the device API. It is protected
by: short expiry, single use enforced by a conditional UPDATE (so two
devices racing cannot both win), a per-token attempt limit, and rate limits
on both the client address and the presented secret.

The response contains the device's own credential. It is not a parent token
and carries no parent permissions.

get.summary: List devices the caller may see
get.description:
Scoped to the families the caller belongs to *and* holds
``devices.read`` in.

get.summary: Get one device with its reported capabilities
get.description:
``presence`` is derived from ``last_seen_at`` and is explicitly an
inference. Capability and permission rows are device-reported facts.

post.description:
Unlinking takes effect on the device's next API call, whether or not the
device is currently reachable. Pending commands are cancelled so the parent
is not shown work that will never run.

Queue one of a fixed set of typed actions.

Only these types can be requested through the API:
``sync_policies``, ``refresh_device_status``, ``request_usage_sync``,
``request_location_update``. There is no generic execute, shell, install or
capture command, and the payload is validated against a per-type schema.

The command is stored before any push is attempted, so it survives a lost
notification. Supplying ``Idempotency-Key`` makes a retry return the
original command rather than queueing a second one.

get.summary: The command types a parent may request
get.description:
Published so client teams build against the allow-list rather than
guessing. Anything absent here is rejected server-side.

get.summary: Everything set for one child, plus real per-device sync state
get.description:
``device_sync_states`` reflects device acknowledgements only.

``capability_warnings`` names the devices that have told us they cannot
enforce what is configured, so the UI can say so instead of implying the
rules are active everywhere.

post.description:
Saved and queued for synchronisation.

Packages required for emergency calling, device settings, or this app
itself are refused. The response says ``pending_sync``: it does not claim
the app is blocked yet.

patch.description:
``if_revision`` gives optimistic concurrency: supply the revision you
read and the update is rejected if another guardian changed it meanwhile.

post.description:
Schedules carry local wall-clock intent plus an IANA timezone, so a 21:00
bedtime stays 21:00 across a daylight-saving change. Two windows that
overlap on the same weekday inside one policy are rejected.

An end time at or before the start means the window crosses midnight
(a 21:00-07:00 bedtime).

get.description:
Returns an empty list while ``FEATURE_WEBSITE_RESTRICTIONS_ENABLED`` is
false. On Android there is no general, policy-compliant way to filter web
content across every browser, so the feature stays off until the Child App
has a supported implementation. See docs/FEATURE_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md.

get.summary: Aggregated usage for a date range
get.description:
All figures are device-reported.

``days_missing_data`` lists dates no device has reported, and
``data_completeness_note`` is set when the range is incomplete, so a partial
total is never presented as the whole picture.

One entry per reporting device, so a child with two devices shows both
rather than a silently merged total.

parameters.name: local_date

schema.description: Defaults to today in the child's timezone.
schema.title: Local Date

parameters.description: Defaults to today in the child's timezone.

get.description:
Cursor-paginated, newest first.

Scoped to families where the caller holds ``alerts.read``; the cursor is
opaque and carries only sort keys, so it cannot widen that scope.

patch.summary: Acknowledge, resolve or dismiss an alert
patch.description:
Requires ``alerts.manage``. An alert cannot be reopened, so the history
of who closed what stays intact.

post.description:
Only the last six characters of the token are ever returned, so the API
cannot be used to read back a usable push credential.

get.description:
Unset types default to enabled. Security notifications are listed with
``always_delivered: true`` and cannot be turned off.

get.summary: Why location is or is not available
get.description:
Explains the real state per device: feature flag, consent record, the
device's reported capability, and its reported permission. No fabricated
availability.

Every read is written to the audit log, including when it returns
nothing. Coordinates are stored rounded to roughly 110 m.

get.summary: Location history within the retention window
get.description:
History is bounded by ``RETENTION_LOCATION_SAMPLES_DAYS``; older samples
have been deleted, not hidden.

Readable without authentication-specific scope so a signed-out pricing
screen can render; returns an empty list when no plans are configured.

``billing_available: false`` tells the client to hide purchase UI rather
than call an endpoint that will return 503.

post.summary: Start a checkout (requires a configured provider)
post.description:
Returns ``503 INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED`` until a payment provider is
selected. It deliberately does not return a fake checkout URL.

The only path that can change entitlement.

The raw body is read before parsing so the signature is verified over
exactly the bytes the provider signed. Verification covers the HMAC and a
timestamp tolerance (replay protection), and
``(provider, provider_event_id)`` is unique, so a retried delivery is
recognised as a duplicate instead of being applied twice.

get.description:
Every record pins the exact policy version that was presented, so what
was agreed and when stays auditable.

post.summary: Record a consent or disclosure acceptance
post.description:
Granting ``location_collection`` here is a precondition for the location
module; it does not by itself enable the feature, which also needs
``FEATURE_LOCATION_ENABLED`` and a device-reported permission.

delete.description:
Withdrawing location consent deletes the samples it authorised.

Consent is not a flag that merely stops future collection; the data
collected under it goes too.

post.summary: Request a data export or deletion
post.description:
An existing open request of the same type is returned rather than
duplicated. ``retention_exceptions`` states plainly what will be kept and
why.

get.description:
Returns the export inline.

Object storage is not configured in this release, so there is no signed
download URL; the same payload would be written to a private bucket once it
is. Per-child usage and location remain available through their own
endpoints while the account is active.

post.description:
Requires the account password and an explicit confirmation phrase.

Devices are unlinked immediately, so monitoring stops now. The data itself
is erased after a grace period, during which the request can be cancelled -
which matters if the request came from someone who should not have had
access.

Devices are not automatically re-linked: they must be paired again,
because their credentials were revoked.

Exchange an access token for a ticket usable only on the WebSocket route.

The ticket carries the authorised family ids as scopes, so the socket does
not have to trust anything the client sends after connecting.

Rotate the device session.

The presented refresh token is consumed. Replaying it revokes the whole
token family, which is how a cloned or extracted credential is contained.
The Child App must store these in Android Keystore-backed storage, never in
plain SharedPreferences.

Ends the presented session only. A device cannot unlink itself from the
family: that is a parent action, so a child cannot end supervision from the
device.

get.summary: Who this device credential belongs to

post.description: Idempotent. Safe to call on every app start.

post.summary: Report that the device is alive
post.description:
The response tells the device whether to fetch policies or commands, so
one call replaces several polls.

post.summary: Report what this device can do
post.description:
The server never assumes a capability. Anything not reported as
``supported`` with a usable permission state is surfaced to the parent as
unsupported rather than silently treated as working.

A permission moving from granted to denied raises a parent alert, because
that is the common way enforcement silently stops working.

get.description:
Precedence is already resolved server-side.

The device applies this document and reports the outcome; it never has to
reconcile overlapping rules itself.

A successful fetch is the only honest "delivered" signal.

A push receipt means the provider accepted a message, not that the device
got it, so ``delivered`` is recorded here rather than at send time.

post.description:
Safe to retry: a repeated acknowledgement is reported as a duplicate and
never overwrites a terminal state.

``unsupported`` and ``permission_denied`` are stored exactly as reported.

They are never translated into success, because a parent being told a rule
is active when it is not is the worst failure this product can have.
Upsert: re-sending a day replaces its totals, so retries are safe.

Backfill after a period offline. Implausible or out-of-window days are
rejected individually and reported, rather than failing the whole batch.

Deduplicated by ``deduplication_key``, so a retried batch is a no-op.

Payloads carrying message content, browsing history, media or coordinates
are rejected: those are outside this product's collection scope.

Accepted only when the feature is enabled, consent is on record, and the
device reports the permission as granted.

A rejected sample returns ``accepted: false`` with a ``rejection_code``;
nothing is stored and no location is fabricated.

A separate identity, session table and token audience from the parent
API, so an admin credential is never interchangeable with a parent one.

In production MFA is asserted by the identity provider or reverse proxy in
front of this API; the session records whether it was satisfied. There is no
server-side TOTP verifier here, and none is faked. See docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.

get.summary: The signed-in admin and their effective permissions

get.description:
Published so the dashboard can build its own permission-aware UI instead
of hard-coding role names.

Aggregates only; no per-account data, so this is safe for every role
that can see the dashboard at all.

The search itself is audited: who searched for what is part of the
support-access trail.

``timezone`` and other profile detail are withheld unless the caller holds
``users.pii.read``.

patch.description:
A reason is mandatory and is stored with the actor's identity.
Suspending or deactivating also signs the account out everywhere.

get.description:
Device metadata only. No usage figures and no location: those require
``child_usage.read`` / ``child_location.read``.

post.description:
Used when a device must be unlinked without the account holder, for
example on a confirmed non-consensual-monitoring report.

get.description:
Non-consensual monitoring is the central abuse risk for a
parental-control product and has its own report category.

patch.description:
``resolution_notes`` is mandatory: a safety decision has to be
documented, not just applied.

get.description: Billing staff see subscription state and nothing about child telemetry.
Reading the audit log is itself audited.

Aggregates across the platform. Includes the command failure and push
failure rates, which are the two numbers that actually predict whether
parents are being told the truth about their devices.

resolution_notes.title: Resolution Notes
resolution_notes.description: Mandatory record of the documented safety decision.

AdminAnalyticsSummaryOut.title: AdminAnalyticsSummaryOut
AdminAnalyticsSummaryOut.description: Aggregates only. Every number is a count over the whole platform.

AdminOverviewOut.title: AdminOverviewOut
AdminOverviewOut.description: Aggregated counts only; no per-account data.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Mandatory. Written to the audit log with the actor identity.

AgeBand.title: AgeBand
AgeBand.description: Coarse age bands. Full dates of birth are deliberately not collected.

device_id.title: Device Id
device_id.description: Scope to a single device. Omit to apply to every device of the child.

if_revision.title: If Revision
if_revision.description: Reject the update unless the stored revision matches.

CapabilityKey.title: CapabilityKey

CapabilitySupport.title: CapabilitySupport
CapabilitySupport.description: Whether the *device* reports it can perform a capability at all.

profile_status.description: Only `active` and `inactive` may be set here; use DELETE to deactivate.

received_at.title: Received At
received_at.description: Device clock; the server records its own receipt time too.

CommandAcknowledgeRequest.title: CommandAcknowledgeRequest
CommandAcknowledgeRequest.description: Sent by the device when it has received a command and begun work.

expires_in_seconds.title: Expires In Seconds
expires_in_seconds.description: Defaults to COMMAND_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS. A command never pends forever.

CommandResult.title: CommandResult
CommandResult.description: What a device reports after attempting a command.

message.title: Message
message.description: Safe, user-displayable explanation. No stack traces or PII.

CommandResultRequest.title: CommandResultRequest
CommandResultRequest.description:
Sent by the device when a command reaches a terminal outcome.

``unsupported`` and ``permission_denied`` are first-class results and are
stored as-is. They are never translated into success.

CommandType.title: CommandType
CommandType.description:
Strict allow-list. No generic execute/shell/capture command exists, and
none may be added: see rule 13/14 in the master prompt.

DailySummarySubmit.title: DailySummarySubmit
DailySummarySubmit.description:
One day of aggregate usage, as computed on the device.

This is *device-reported* data. It is validated for plausibility and
labelled as reported throughout the API; the server cannot and does not
claim it is cryptographically proven.

DeviceCommandOut.title: DeviceCommandOut
DeviceCommandOut.description: Device-facing projection: no parent identity, no family metadata.

presence.title: Presence
presence.description: online | recently_seen | offline | unknown, derived from last_seen_at.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: Safe context only: package identifiers, counts, enum values. Never message content, keystrokes, screenshots or coordinates.

presence.title: Presence
presence.description: online | recently_seen | offline | unknown, derived from last_seen_at.

DevicePolicySnapshot.title: DevicePolicySnapshot
DevicePolicySnapshot.description:
The authoritative, device-scoped policy document.

The Child App applies this and reports back with
``POST /device/commands/{id}/result`` including ``applied_policy_version``.
Precedence is already resolved server-side, so the device does not have to
reason about overlapping policies.

DeviceRegisterRequest.title: DeviceRegisterRequest
DeviceRegisterRequest.description: Completes or refreshes registration using the device's own credential.

DeviceRegistrationInfo.title: DeviceRegistrationInfo
DeviceRegistrationInfo.description:
Minimal device metadata.

Deliberately excluded: hardware serial, IMEI, MAC address, advertising id,
phone number, installed-app inventory. None of those are needed for the
product and all of them increase harm if breached.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Recorded in the audit log and shown in the device history.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: Permissions to grant. Omit for the default guardian set. Family restructuring, billing and privacy permissions cannot be delegated.

availability.title: Availability
availability.description: One of: available, feature_disabled, consent_missing, permission_denied, unsupported.

LocationStatusOut.title: LocationStatusOut
LocationStatusOut.description: Why location is or is not available, without fabricating data.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page.

total.title: Total
total.description: Only populated for endpoints where an exact count is cheap.

PageInfo.title: PageInfo
PageInfo.description: Cursor pagination metadata. Cursors are opaque and must not be parsed.

disclosure_version.title: Disclosure Version
disclosure_version.description: Version of the on-device disclosure the user acknowledged.

disclosure_acknowledged.title: Disclosure Acknowledged
disclosure_acknowledged.description: Must be true. The Child App shows the disclosure before claiming.

device_label.title: Device Label
device_label.description: Optional label applied to the device once it pairs.

include_short_code.title: Include Short Code
include_short_code.description: Also issue a short, human-typable code alongside the QR token.

PairingInvitationCreated.title: PairingInvitationCreated
PairingInvitationCreated.description:
Returned once, at creation time only.

``claim_token`` is the value to encode in the QR code. The server stores
only its hash, so it can never be retrieved again and is never logged.
Do **not** encode a parent JWT or account details in the QR payload.

PermissionState.title: PermissionState
PermissionState.description: Android runtime/special permission state, as reported by the device.

PolicyBundleOut.title: PolicyBundleOut
PolicyBundleOut.description: Everything the Parent App needs to render a child's policy screen.

PolicyMutationResult.title: PolicyMutationResult
PolicyMutationResult.description:
Returned by every policy mutation.

``sync_status`` is always ``pending_sync`` immediately after a change: the
server has saved the intent and queued a sync, and it does not claim the
device has applied anything until the device says so.

family_id.title: Family Id
family_id.description: Required for a family-scoped export; omit for an account-wide request.

RealtimeTicketOut.title: RealtimeTicketOut
RealtimeTicketOut.description:
Short-lived ticket for the WebSocket handshake.

Browsers cannot set an ``Authorization`` header on a WebSocket, so the
client exchanges its access token for a single-purpose ticket (audience
``cdc:ws``, ~60s lifetime) and passes it as a query parameter.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Shown to the child on the device and stored in the audit log.

RequestLocationUpdatePayload.title: RequestLocationUpdatePayload
RequestLocationUpdatePayload.description:
Only accepted when the location feature is enabled, consent is on record
and the device reports the permission as granted. Rejected otherwise.

RevokeDevicePayload.title: RevokeDevicePayload
RevokeDevicePayload.description: Server-generated only; a parent revokes via ``POST /devices/{id}/revoke``.

if_revision.title: If Revision
if_revision.description: Reject the update unless the stored revision matches.

if_revision.title: If Revision
if_revision.description: Reject the update unless the stored revision matches.

SyncStatus.title: SyncStatus
SyncStatus.description:
What the *server knows* about device application of a policy set.

Never inferred: only moved forward by a device acknowledgement/result.

BearerAuth.description: Access token from the matching login endpoint. Parent, device and admin tokens are not interchangeable.
